$comment: Machine-readable per-provider reference backing docs/providers.md. Every client id and secret below is an obviously fake sandbox value; nothing was registered. Endpoint URLs were verified against provider docs and live discovery/metadata documents in November 2026; each provider lists its source pages.

endpoints.notes: Revocation: POST with token=<access-or-refresh-token>, empty 200. ID token iss=https://accounts.google.com, user key is sub, never email.

scopes.refresh_token_gate: access_type=offline; refresh token issued only on first consent

ios.rule: Custom scheme: reversed client id (com.googleusercontent.apps.<prefix>) or own reverse-domain scheme containing a period. Loopback blocked for iOS client types.

android.rule: No redirect: loopback and custom schemes are blocked for Android client types. Client is registered by package name + SHA-1; sanctioned path is the native SDK handing back a server auth code.

desktop.rule: Loopback http://127.0.0.1:{random free port} (or [::1]); register http://127.0.0.1. localhost works but is warned against. Loopback stays supported for desktop client types.

web.rule: Registered https redirect URI, exact match (redirect_uri_mismatch otherwise).

quirks: Embedded webviews are rejected with disallowed_useragent; use the system browser (SFSafariViewController is acceptable).
PKCE always; code_challenge_method defaults to plain if omitted, so send S256 explicitly.
client_secret optional for installed apps; never embed one.
Refresh token only on first consent, only with access_type=offline; caps per client/user, oldest silently invalidated.
Loopback IP flow blocked for iOS/Android/Chrome client types (all clients since 2022-10-21).
registration: console.cloud.google.com -> APIs & Services -> OAuth consent screen: app name, support email, scopes openid / .../auth/userinfo.profile / .../auth/userinfo.email.

Credentials -> Create credentials -> OAuth client ID, one client per surface: Web application (https redirect), Desktop app (http://127.0.0.1), iOS (bundle id, derives com.googleusercontent.apps scheme), Android (package + SHA-1).
Copy client id, e.g. fake nsh-auth-sandbox.apps.googleusercontent.com. Desktop/iOS clients have no secret; web secrets belong on the broker.

brand.label: Sign in with Google
brand.shape: rectangular or pill, keep aspect ratio
brand.logo: standard multicolor G, never recolored; padding 12/10/12 px (web/android), 16/12/16 (ios)
brand.placement: at least as prominent as other sign-in options

endpoints.notes: Version pin per release (docs sampled show v27.0). Discovery declares issuer https://www.facebook.com, RS256, implicit-only response types, no token endpoint. Access tokens are opaque; only the OIDC variant yields a JWT id_token.

authorize_extras.nonce: required in the OIDC code flow

scopes.refresh_token_gate: no documented refresh token; short-lived tokens, re-authenticate on expiry

client.client_secret_required_at_exchange: required in the classic manual flow; optional in the OIDC code flow only when code_verifier is sent
client.pkce: code_challenge required in OIDC flow; S256 recommended, plain is the default when omitted

ios.rule: No documented custom-scheme redirect for the manual flow; the sanctioned native path is the Facebook SDK (fb{app-id}:// internally) or an https relay. Desktop webview shape uses https://www.facebook.com/connect/login_success.html with response_type=token.

android.rule: Same as iOS: SDK path or https relay; manual flow documents no custom scheme. Legacy Windows broker: ms-app://{package-security-identifier}.

desktop.rule: https redirect or the login_success.html implicit shape; Valid OAuth Redirect URIs + Enforce HTTPS + Strict Mode apply.

web.rule: Registered https redirect URI under Facebook Login -> Settings -> Valid OAuth Redirect URIs; Enforce HTTPS required; Strict Mode requires exact string match (state is the only ignored extra). Development mode tolerates unregistered localhost, a dashboard behavior not in the docs.

quirks: Two documented flow shapes: classic manual flow (client_secret required, server-to-server) vs OIDC code flow (client_secret optional with code_verifier). nsh-auth uses OIDC+PKCE for public clients, classic via the broker.
No RFC 7009 revocation endpoint; revoke grants via DELETE /{version}/me/permissions or the dashboard deauthorize callback.
URLs are versioned ({version}); version is provider config.
With Require App Secret enabled, Graph calls need appsecret_proof (HMAC-SHA256 of the token with the app secret).
Enforce HTTPS (all OAuth redirects) and Strict Mode (exact redirect match) are mandatory for all apps.
email is optional for users and may be absent even when granted.
registration: developers.facebook.com -> My Apps -> Create App (Authentication).
Add the Facebook Login product; Facebook Login -> Settings -> Valid OAuth Redirect URIs, e.g. fake https://demo.example.com/callback/facebook; keep Enforce HTTPS and Strict Mode on.
App Settings -> Basic: App ID (fake 1234567890123456) and App Secret (fake nsh-sandbox-app-secret-not-real); secret goes to the broker.
Add the domain under Settings -> Basic -> App Domains; stay in Development mode while testing.

brand.label: Continue with Facebook

primary.note: button blue per the UX page sentence 'Button colors are white and Facebook blue: 5890FF'

brand.font: free choice, must stay legible; no published pixel minimums
brand.logo: approved f logo before the call to action, never recolored or altered; copy inside the button

endpoints.notes: Token endpoint is application/x-www-form-urlencoded ONLY. Response: access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 604800 (7 days), refresh_token, scope. Metadata: issuer https://discord.com, code_challenge_methods_supported [S256], token auth methods basic/post/none, iss parameter on all redirects.

scopes.oidc_scope: openid (ID token, RS256) exists per server metadata but is absent from the docs scopes table
scopes.refresh_token_gate: refresh_token on the authorization_code grant; none for implicit or client_credentials

client.client_secret_required_at_exchange: basic or form client_id/client_secret normally; metadata allows none for PKCE public clients
client.pkce: S256 supported per RFC 8414 metadata but undocumented in prose docs

ios.rule: Register the redirect in the Developer Portal (OAuth2 -> Redirects); docs impose no scheme restriction and document no explicit custom-scheme rule. Confirm the scheme in the portal at registration.

android.rule: Same as iOS: portal-registered redirect, no documented scheme restrictions.

desktop.rule: No documented loopback rules; loopback is a possible portal-registered redirect, otherwise use a custom scheme.

web.rule: Portal-registered https redirect URI, sent URL-encoded as redirect_uri.

quirks: Every authorization redirect carries iss=https://discord.com (RFC 9207); validate before exchanging the code.
token/revoke revokes the entire authorization (all tokens for the grant) regardless of token_type_hint.
Token endpoint accepts x-www-form-urlencoded only; JSON is rejected.
expires_in is 604800 (7-day access tokens).
Implicit grant returns parameters in URL fragments, not query strings.
openid scope and PKCE are under-documented (metadata yes, prose no); prefer identify+email /users/@me as the identity source.
registration: discord.com/developers/applications -> New Application.
OAuth2: copy Client ID (fake 1122334455667788990); Reset Secret for the Client Secret (fake nsh-sandbox-discord-secret), shown once.
OAuth2 -> Redirects: add per surface, e.g. fake https://demo.example.com/callback/discord and com.nshauth.sandbox:/oauth2redirect.
Public sign-in needs only the Client ID; the secret is for broker/confidential use.

brand.label: Continue with Discord
brand.logo: do not edit, change, distort, recolor, or reconfigure; color/black/white variants only; digital use only
brand.placement: no official button spec; keep parity with the other provider buttons

endpoints.notes: No OIDC artifacts at all. Code expires after 10 minutes. Token endpoint returns form-encoded by default; send Accept: application/json for JSON. Check/reset/revoke are POST/PATCH/DELETE /applications/{client_id}/token with access_token in the request body, all Basic auth client_id:client_secret.

scopes.minimal_alternative: no scope at all grants read-only public profile via /user
scopes.refresh_token_gate: offline_access (or expiring-tokens enabled on the app): access token 8h, refresh token 6 months of disuse, rotation on use

client.pkce: S256 supported and strongly recommended; plain unsupported; does not remove the client_secret requirement

ios.rule: No documented custom-scheme callback. Mobile goes through the token broker (https callback on the owner's server that relays to the app) or the device flow (no redirect).

android.rule: Same as iOS: broker or device flow; no documented custom-scheme callback.

desktop.rule: Loopback supported: redirect_uri on http://127.0.0.1:{any port} or [::1] need not match the registered port; use 127.0.0.1/::1, not localhost.

web.rule: Registered https callback URL (up to 10 per app); host and port must match exactly, path may be a subdirectory, optional per-URL wildcard subdomain.

quirks: client_secret required on the code exchange (web application flow); only the device flow omits it -> token broker is mandatory for in-app sign-in.
Rotating refresh tokens: a used refresh token is invalidated and replaced; refreshing cannot widen scopes.
Token check/reset/revoke require Basic auth with the client secret, so they are broker-side operations.
Identity is the REST /user call; no ID token to verify; user id is the stable key.
GitHub recommends GitHub Apps over OAuth Apps for new integrations; nsh-auth ships the OAuth App flow as it fits user sign-in.
registration: GitHub -> Settings -> Developer settings -> OAuth Apps -> New OAuth App.
Fill application name, homepage URL, and the Authorization callback URL (one per surface, up to 10), e.g. fake https://broker.example.com/callback/github.
Copy the Client ID (fake Ov23linshsandbox0000000) and generate the Client Secret (fake nsh-sandbox-gh-secret), shown once; it goes into broker config only.
Optional: enable Expire user authorization tokens for the refresh-token behavior.

brand.label: Sign in with GitHub

themes.alternate: white fill with the black mark

brand.logo: Invertocat in white, black, or (few cases) grey/green; never compress, distort, skew, stretch, or alter; keep contrast
brand.placement: do not imply GitHub endorsement; logo only for GitHub sign-in/integration

endpoints.notes: Discovery: issuer https://appleid.apple.com, scopes openid/email/name, response_modes query/fragment/form_post, token auth client_secret_post, RS256. Grant types authorization_code and refresh_token. Code is single-use, 5-minute validity. Identity rides in the id_token; name/email also arrive as a user field on the first authorization POST.

scopes.refresh_token_gate: refresh tokens issued at exchange via grant_type=refresh_token; no fixed expiry but invalidated out-of-band (password/email change)

client.client_secret_format: ES256 JWT made by the owner: header {alg: ES256, kid: Key ID}, payload {iss: Team ID, iat, exp <= iat+15777000, aud: https://appleid.apple.com, sub: client_id}, signed with the account .p8 key -> lives in the broker
client.pkce: not applicable; client_secret JWT is the client authentication

ios.rule: Prefer ASAuthorizationController (system flow, no HTTP redirect). The web-based path still needs an https redirect_uri; Apple does not accept custom schemes or IPs/localhost.

android.rule: https redirect_uri only (Services ID Return URL); the relay page must send the user back to the app; no custom scheme, IP, or localhost accepted.

desktop.rule: https redirect_uri registered as Return URL; ASWebAuthenticationSession can start the flow but the result arrives as a POST to the https relay.

web.rule: Registered https Return URL, domain-based, no fragment; response_mode=form_post whenever scopes are requested: code, id_token, state, and first-time user arrive as application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST body fields.

quirks: client_secret is a self-made ES256 JWT (max exp 15777000 seconds, about six months) signed with the account .p8 key; the key is a credential and belongs in the broker.
form_post + POST-body identity: loopback and custom schemes cannot receive the response; only a real https endpoint can. Server must relay control back to the app.
name and email are delivered only on the first authorization (user POST field); persist at first sign-in.
user_cancelled_authorize is the only error Apple may POST back; treat as cancel.
Revocation (/auth/revoke with token, client_id, client_secret, token_type_hint) is required by App Store rules on account deletion.
Handle invalid_grant on refresh by re-running the authorization flow.
id_token RS256, iss https://appleid.apple.com, aud = client_id, sub = stable per-developer user id.
registration: developer.apple.com -> Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles -> Identifiers: App ID with the Sign In with Apple capability (native flow).
Register a Services ID (fake com.nshauth.sandbox), enable Sign In with Apple, set the primary domain and Return URLs (fake https://demo.example.com/callback/apple).

Keys -> Create a Key with Sign In with Apple; download the .p8 and note the 10-char Key ID; note the Team ID (fake NSHSANDBX01). Services ID + Team ID + Key ID + .p8 are the broker inputs for minting client_secret JWTs.

brand.label: Sign in with Apple
brand.logo: apple.logo SF Symbol, height = button height; title font = 43% of button height (44pt -> 19pt); logo-only button is 1:1, no crop
brand.text_rules: black or white only, no custom colors; capitalization preserved (first word + Apple capitalized)
brand.shape: corner radius adjustable: rounded (default), square, capsule

endpoints.notes: No RFC 7009 revocation endpoint; sign-out is local token destruction plus the OIDC end-session request (post_logout_redirect_uri must be registered). Access tokens ~1h (expires_in 3599).

scopes.refresh_token_gate: offline_access must be requested explicitly or no refresh token is issued
scopes.notes: Scopes are resource-prefixed (User.Read = Graph); a mixed-resource token request collapses to the first resource.

client.client_secret_required_at_exchange: only for confidential web apps; native/SPA must not use secrets (private_key_jwt or certificate credentials are the confidential alternative)
client.pkce: recommended for all client types; required for SPA; S256 and plain both accepted

ios.rule: iOS/macOS or Mobile-and-desktop platform type; custom schemes supported (msal{client-id}://auth is generated for the mobile platform).

android.rule: Android platform type with the package/scheme binding MSAL generates.

desktop.rule: Loopback per RFC 8252: http://localhost:{any port}, port ignored when matching; Microsoft recommends 127.0.0.1 over localhost. The portal text box rejects http://127.0.0.1 (add via manifest replyUrlsWithType); [::1] unsupported. Embedded-webview fallback: https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/nativeclient. form_post recommended with localhost.

web.rule: https URI; SPA code+PKCE needs the URI registered as type SPA (web type fails CORS redemption). URIs case-sensitive, <= 256 chars, 256 total (100 with personal accounts in audience), no fragments/IDN/special chars ! $ ' ( ) , ;.

quirks: Tenant scoping is in the URL path: common / organizations / consumers / tenant-id; guest cross-tenant sign-in must use the target tenant id.
offline_access explicit; refresh tokens are not revoked on use (rotate and discard); spa-type redirect URIs get 24h refresh tokens.
No revocation endpoint: sign-out = drop local tokens + OIDC logout request.
ID-token issuance must be enabled in the registration for response_type containing id_token (implicit/hybrid); the code flow returns the id_token from the token endpoint when openid was requested.
Graph access tokens are opaque/encrypted (especially for personal accounts): never parse tokens for APIs you do not own; use the ID token for identity.
response_mode: query for code-only, fragment/form_post when an id_token rides along; form_post recommended for reliability and localhost.
registration: entra.microsoft.com -> Microsoft Entra ID -> App registrations -> New registration; pick the account audience (e.g. any organizational directory + personal Microsoft accounts).
Copy the Application (client) ID (fake 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555).
Authentication -> Add a platform per surface: Web (https redirect), Single-page application (same URI, SPA type), Mobile and desktop applications / Android / iOS (custom scheme).
Authentication -> Advanced settings: enable Allow public client flows = Yes for the secretless native flow.
Confidential/broker deployments add a credential under Certificates & secrets.

brand.label: Sign in with Microsoft

themes.note: light and dark schemes; use the official downloadable button SVGs and redlines as the reference; no hex values published on the guidelines page

brand.font: follow the redlines with the official assets; embed the official SVG symbol in the hand-built button
brand.logo: four-square Microsoft symbol exactly as published; do not alter; its pairing with the wording is what represents the platform
copy_rules: never say Azure AD, Microsoft 365 ID, enterprise account, or corporate account in UI copy
use work or school account for Entra accounts

endpoints.notes: Not OIDC: no id_token, JWKS, or discovery. Authorize params: response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri (exact match), scope, state <= 500 chars, code_challenge, code_challenge_method S256|plain. Token endpoint form-encoded; public clients send client_id in the body, confidential use a Basic header. Code expires in 30 seconds; access tokens live 2 hours without offline.access.

scopes.refresh_token_gate: offline.access: no refresh token without it

client.client_secret_required_at_exchange: public clients (Native App / SPA app types) get no secret and use PKCE only; confidential clients (Web App / Automated App) use a Basic header
client.pkce: required for public clients, present on all documented examples; S256 preferred over plain

ios.rule: Native App is a public client type; callback URLs are allowlisted in the console with exact match incl. trailing slashes, max 10. Custom schemes are not documented either way; register and verify, or use an https relay.

desktop.rule: Allowlisted http://127.0.0.1 callback; docs recommend 127.0.0.1 over localhost for local development.

web.rule: Allowlisted https callback URL; javascript:, data:, file:, ftp:, mailto:, telnet: and similar schemes are disallowed.

quirks: PKCE-only for public clients; the flow is literally named Authorization Code Flow with PKCE.
No OIDC: identity is the REST /2/users/me call over TLS; no ID token to verify.
Refresh tokens gated by offline.access; rotate at the same token endpoint (grant_type=refresh_token).
30-second authorization code lifetime: exchange immediately.
Public vs confidential is fixed by app type chosen in the console; credentials are shown once.
Revoke takes token (+ client_id or Basic header).
registration: console.x.com -> create a Project and an App.

Settings -> User authentication settings -> Set up: enable OAuth 2.0, choose app type Native App (public) or Web App (confidential), set Read or Read-and-write, enter Callback URI(s) (fake https://demo.example.com/callback/x) and a Website URL.
Copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID (fake bnNoLXNhbmRib3gtbm90LXJlYWwwMDAwMDAwMDoxOmNp, decodes to nsh-sandbox-not-real00000000:1:ci) and Client Secret for confidential apps; shown once.

brand.label: Continue with X
brand.logo: the X logo may not be altered; black/white treatments; details live in the toolkit's trademark/brand guidelines
brand.placement: mark only to indicate X sign-in; do not imply endorsement

endpoints.notes: Read behavior from metadata: code_challenge_methods_supported, token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported (none = public clients OK), id_token_signing_alg_values_supported, scopes_supported, authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, issuer.

scopes.refresh_token_gate: offline_access when the provider gates refresh tokens on it; check scopes_supported

client.client_secret_required_at_exchange: depends on token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported; use none for public clients when listed
client.pkce: S256 always, if the server lists S256

ios.rule: RFC 8252 custom scheme in reverse-domain form (period recommended), declared to the host so the OS routes it back; some providers require an exact registered scheme+path.

android.rule: Same as iOS via the Android intent filter.

desktop.rule: RFC 8252 loopback http://127.0.0.1:{random free port}; port matching is provider-specific (some ignore it).

quirks: Follow the metadata: only send code_challenge_method values the server lists; pick client auth from token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported; verify iss when authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported is true.
Validate the id_token against jwks_uri with the advertised signing algs; check iss == discovery issuer, aud == client_id, exp/iat, nonce.
A provider with no userinfo_endpoint and no openid scope is plain OAuth 2.0: identity comes from an /me-style REST call configured by the owner.
registration: Create an OAuth client in the provider's console.
Register one redirect URI per surface (fake https://demo.example.com/callback/oidc, com.nshauth.sandbox:/oauth2redirect, loopback for desktop).
Obtain client_id (+ client_secret only for confidential deployments) and enter the issuer URL in nsh-auth config; discovery is fetched at runtime.

themes.note: no brand rules for a generic provider; render a neutral secondary button in the host app palette
